subject: Request: Rebate carveout & tactical discount for BrightScale bridge deployment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Clarke <aaron@brightscale.com>, Contracts (BrightScale) <contracts@brightscale.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Rebate carveout & tactical discount for BrightScale bridge deployment

Team — quick escalation request. BrightScale (Aaron) is ready to move to a 3‑year committed package (dedicated VPC + private control plane) but is pushing hard on upfront economics. They have two competing offers that are close on headline price; it’s become clear that our standard public rate card + onboarding credit won’t win this.

Why this matters: BrightScale is a strategic healthcare analytics platform — strong reference potential in payer space and native multi‑region requirements (they want EU + US). If we lose, they’re likely to pick a competitor with weaker observability and higher long‑term unit cost but better short‑term concession.

What I’m asking for: a one‑time onboarding credit and a short‑term rebate/carveout to bridge the first 12 months. Concretely I’m proposing the pricing model attached (BS_pricing_model_3yr.xlsx):
- One‑time onboarding credit: $150,000 (applied to SOW/first invoice)
- Recurring rebate: 18% effective discount on recurring consumption for months 0–12 only
- Standard rate card thereafter (months 13+) with commitment floors written into contract

Attachments: BrightScale_MutualActionPlan_v2.pdf, BS_pricing_model_3yr.xlsx, customer_quote_BS-2026-03.pdf (quote shows how the concession compares vs. public rates).

Why this is conservative: the proposed structure is time‑limited and tied to committed ARR (proposed threshold $1.2M ARR over 12 months). It preserves long‑term economics and keeps pricing aligned after year 1. Sales is prepared to include a 60‑day clawback for churn within the first 6 months.

Timing: Aaron has signoff from his procurement lead and wants a final commercial term sheet by EOD Friday to present to his board next Tuesday. If we can get VP/CFO conditional signoff now, Legal can draft quickly and Contracts can route DocuSign.

Request: marissa — can you validate revenue treatment & risk (deferred revenue/clawback)? kimberly — would you consider one of the following: (A) full approve the one‑time $150k + 18% rebate for 12 months with the ARR threshold and clawback, or (B) approve a reduced onboarding credit ($125k) + 18% rebate? Either gets us over the line.

I’m available to jump on a quick call with finance/legal to walk through the attachment.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415‑555‑0192

(Attachments: BrightScale_MutualActionPlan_v2.pdf; BS_pricing_model_3yr.xlsx; customer_quote_BS-2026-03.pdf)

Subject: Re: Request: Rebate carveout & tactical discount for BrightScale bridge deployment

Jonas — thanks for the write up and the attachments. A couple quick asks before Mary/Finance greenlights:
- Please call out the expected ARR and month‑by‑month consumption profile in the pricing model (I don’t see the MRR ramp in the XLS). Need to confirm we’re not building a long tail hole that negates the commitment.
- Confirm how the onboarding credit is applied (invoice credit vs. prepaid service credit) and whether it nets against deferred revenue.
- If Legal is going to accept the 60‑day clawback, we need explicit churn triggers and a defined clawback schedule in the MAP.

If those items are clean, I’ll validate revenue recognition treatment and flag any policy exceptions. We’ll want to keep executive approvals in this thread.

—Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Marissa — thanks. Updated the attached pricing workbook to include a monthly consumption ramp and ARR math (see tab "Ramp & ARR" in BS_pricing_model_3yr.xlsx). Key bullets here so execs can decide quickly:
- Committed ARR (year 1): $1.35M based on conservative ramp (50% of committed capacity in Q1, 80% by Q3).
- NPV impact to Redwood (12 months with proposed concessions): ~‑$98k vs. baseline; lifetime (3yr) still net positive revenue compared to competitor because we preserve standard pricing after month 12.
- Strategic optionality: BrightScale will reference us in a payer proof that could accelerate sales motions in two major accounts — estimated pipeline influence $3.4M ARR over 18 months if win occurs.

Updated ask (refined after internal ops check):
- One‑time onboarding credit: $150k (sales willing to accept $125k if necessary; see two scenarios in the "Quote" tab)
- Recurring rebate: 18% months 0–12 only, tied to committed ARR >= $1.2M; rebate void if ARR falls below threshold after month 3 (clawback triggers apply).

We need Kimberly’s signoff on the commercial concession or direction to reduce the onboarding credit. I’ve included the HubSpot link for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BS-2026-03-ARC (contains underwriting notes and procurement email chain).

If approved I’ll instruct SalesOps to push the updated quote and route DocuSign (link included in metadata). Aaron — appreciate the patience; expecting legal to tighten the MSA language around clawback.

—Jonas

Thanks for the thoughtful packet, Jonas. I have reviewed the updated ramp and NPV scenarios. I will grant conditional approval with the following requirements:

1) Approve: 18% recurring rebate for months 0–12 and a one‑time onboarding credit of $125,000 (reduced from $150k)
2) Commercial conditions to be included in the SOW/MSA: committed ARR threshold of $1.2M for rebate eligibility, explicit 60‑day clawback schedule (pro rata), and a termination clause that triggers full repay of onboarding credit if customer cancels within first 3 months.
3) Revenue recognition: Marissa to confirm by EOD tomorrow on whether the $125k onboarding credit needs to be deferred and amortized (expected answer: yes, with monthly release tied to consumption).
4) Legal/Contracts: include explicit clawback language and ensure the rebate is time‑boxed in the schedule. Contracts must attach a short schedule that enumerates the clawback calculation.

Jonas — please update the quote to reflect the $125k onboarding credit and provide an updated customer_quote_BS-2026-03.pdf. Once updated, route to me and Marissa for final signoff and route via DocuSign.

This approval is conditional on Legal & Revenue Ops implementing the controls above.

—Kimberly Park
VP Finance | Redwood Inference
